title: A Flow Matching Algorithm for Many-Shot Adaptation to Unseen Distributions
abstract: arXiv:2605.06272v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: While generative modeling has achieved remarkable success on tasks like natural language-conditioned image generation, enabling model adaptation from example data points remains a relatively underexplored and challenging problem. To this end, we propose Function Projection for Flow Matching (FP-FM), an algorithm that directly conditions generation on samples from the target distribution. FP-FM learns basis functions to span the velocity fields corresponding to a set of training distributions, and adapts to new distributions by computing a simple least-squares projection onto this basis. This enables efficient generation of samples from diverse target distributions without additional training at inference time. We further introduce multiple variants of FP-FM that provide a trade-off in expressivity and compute by enriching the coefficient calculation, e.g., by making the coefficients dependent on time. translated_title: 一种用于未见分布多样本适应的流匹配算法
translated_abstract: 尽管生成建模在自然语言条件图像生成等任务上取得了显著成功，但如何使模型从示例数据点进行适应仍然是一个相对探索不足且具有挑战性的问题。为此，我们提出了流匹配函数投影，这是一种直接以目标分布样本为条件进行生成的算法。FP-FM 学习基函数来张成与一组训练分布相对应的速度场，并通过计算到该基的简单最小二乘投影来适应新分布。这使得在推理时无需额外训练即可高效地从各种目标分布生成样本。我们进一步引入了 FP-FM 的多种变体，通过丰富系数计算（例如使系数依赖于时间）来在表达能力与计算量之间提供权衡。FP-FM 实现了大幅提升的
tldr: 提出流匹配函数投影（FP-FM）算法，通过学习速度场的基函数并以最小二乘投影方式适应新分布，无需推理时额外训练即可基于少量样本实现对未见目标分布的高效生成。
en_tdlr: Proposes Function Projection for Flow Matching (FP-FM), which adapts to unseen target distributions from example samples by learning basis functions spanning velocity fields and computing simple least-squares projections, enabling efficient generation without additional training at inference time.
